title: they-one / they-many — say whether ‘they’ is one actor or several
problem: they-one / they-many — say whether they refers to one person or entity, or several
rationale: The same English subject pronoun can refer to one person or entity or several, which can leave a quoted operational message without enough information to select the correct next action. The proposal makes referent number explicit while keeping identity and group-action semantics separate. This prospective version seeks actual token savings relative to a complete careful-English expansion with demonstrated comprehension preservation, not an artificial accuracy advantage created by counting a justified clarification of bare they as an error. It makes no claim that existing cold models represent future Ainglish-trained models or human comprehension. Future training and tokenizer inclusion are separate hypotheses, not evidence that a current cold-use failure has passed.
english_mapping: The complete per-form subject expansions are: they-one = "that one person or entity"; they-many = "those two or more people or entities". they-one is singular they and denotes exactly one referent person or entity; they-many is plural they and denotes two or more referent people or entities. Both take ordinary they agreement. The number is the number of referents, not a count of the people represented by an entity such as a committee. The marker alone specifies neither gender nor which antecedent was intended, and does not entail unanimity, participation by every group member, or collective rather than distributive action. Context may separately specify those facts, but the number marker adds none of them.
predicted_measurement: Prospective compactness carrier: token_delta on the same frozen complete messages against the exact per-form careful-English subject expansions, predicting strictly negative least-favourable registered-tokenizer mean cost overall and savings in each form; +1 token is no longer accepted. Reader prerequisite: comprehension_accuracy_delta against meaning-equivalent careful English, with a prespecified 5 percentage-point maximum-loss margin and an approved replayable simultaneous uncertainty method. Require the aggregate and each form lower bound to be at least -5 pp, and marked and careful absolute-accuracy lower bounds at least 90% in each form. Marked unsafe-action upper bounds must be at most 5% in each form. Separately require upper bounds at most 5% for each form-by-nonclaim false inference about gender, known identity, unanimity, all-members participation and collective action, with corresponding shared-context positive-control accuracy lower bounds at least 90%. The study fixes a held-out operational-consequence population, true semantic-world unit/clusters, claim family, two-reader weights, official arm allocation, sample size and operating-characteristic justification before any target exposure. No direct number/definition questions, identity-enriched English or people-count keys inferred from entity count. Bare-they controls have an arm-specific correct clarification/unknown answer whenever the consequence is not determined; report safe-action information gain descriptively, not as a superiority carrier. Use independently reviewed, frozen disjoint worlds for an original and an independently accepted replication, retaining adverse/null results and aborts. A tiny ceiling bootstrap or failure to detect a difference is not preservation. Missing coverage or unresolved bounds leave the claim incomplete; a violated prespecified limit opposes this version. Existing confirmed-loss veto and formal independent ratification gates remain unchanged, even if a loss is within the 5 pp margin. No retrospective evidence relabelling or post-result changes to margin, bank, comparator or teaching condition.
example_ainglish: The notice leaves open which named contact or group is involved. they-one will receive the access request. / The notice leaves open which named contact or group is involved. they-many will receive the access request.
example_english: The notice leaves open which named contact or group is involved. that one person or entity will receive the access request. / The notice leaves open which named contact or group is involved. those two or more people or entities will receive the access request.

slot.they-one: singular they: exactly one referent; no gender claim
slot.they-many: plural they: two or more referents; no all-members, unanimity, or collective-action claim
